subject: Quick sanity check: tokens/$ tradeoffs in MAP and eval plan
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@helixmed.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP: unit cost assumptions — can you confirm?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the MAP draft — procurement asked me to validate the cost line items before we loop legal. A few quick asks so we can lock the eval plan:

- Can you confirm the assumed tokens-per-call for the demo evaluation? The spreadsheet I attached to the MAP has a placeholder (prompt 450 / response 1,200) but we saw large variance in prior pilots.
- How much uplift are you modeling for peak concurrency (we're expecting bursts during triage flows)?
- Does Redwood's caching/prefix KV assumptions reduce tokens billed or only reduce effective latency? That distinction matters for our unit economics.
- If we need private deployment for PHI, how should we adjust the tokens/$ assumptions (or is that a separate pricing line)?

We attached the MAP + our evaluation criteria; procurement would like an updated MAP with the cost sensitivity table before Thursday so we can keep the closing timeline.

Appreciate a short note or a quick sync — Sam

--
Sam Park
Director of Product
HelixMed
[attachment: helixmed_map_req.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@helixmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: unit cost assumptions — can you confirm?

Sam — thanks, got it. Quick answers and a couple clarifying Qs before Ben shares numbers: 

> Can you confirm the assumed tokens-per-call for the demo evaluation?
We used a conservative median in the MAP (prompt ~450, response ~1,000) but that was a placeholder. Can you confirm the typical user flow (single-turn vs multi-turn, average history preserved)? If you expect multi-turn with 3–5 message history we should multiply prompt tokens by the average context size.

> Peak concurrency / burst modeling?
We need a ballpark: light (<=50 r/s), moderate (50–250 r/s), heavy (>250 r/s). Tell us which fits HelixMed's triage windows.

> Caching / billing behavior?
Ben: the short summary you prepared below will help — specifically whether prefix/KV cache reduces billed tokens or just latency.

> PHI / private deployment
Jordan: can you confirm if private (VPC or on-prem) has a different per-token rate baked into the MAP? If not, we'll flag procurement that private infra is an add-on and may change economics.

If it helps, I'm free Friday 09:00–11:30 PT for a 30-min run-through and we can ship an updated MAP same day. I'll attach a starter workbook.

Thanks — tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: MAP-draft-v2.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@helixmed.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: unit cost assumptions — can you confirm?

Hi Sam / team — pulled together the quick unit-econ scan for the MAP. High-level summary (we'll add detail to the spreadsheet):

- Baseline tokens per demo request (current MAP placeholder): prompt = 450 tokens, response = 1,000 tokens => total ~1,450 tokens/request.
- Modal production path (shorter prompts, cached prefixes): prompt = 220, response = 420 => total ~640 tokens/request.
- Caching behavior: prefix/KV caching reduces compute and latency by returning a cached KV state, but billing depends on the cache hit semantics. For Redwood hosted inference: cached prefix hits avoid re-computation and are billed for the *incremental* tokens only (so large prompt prefixes can materially reduce billed tokens). For dedicated/private with strict replay, we can configure to bill on generated tokens only — we will document how the MAP should express this.
- Batching effects: with continuous batching we see per-token unit cost drop 8–22% depending on sequence length and batch size; we recommend modeling a 15% cost improvement for moderate batching (50–150ms queueing).

Tokens-per-dollar guidance (example rates for MAP sensitivity table):
- Conservative: 55k tokens / $1 (assumes small model with higher per-token inference cost, limited batching)
- Typical: 150k tokens / $1 (quantized model with standard batching and prefix caching)
- Optimistic: 380k tokens / $1 (aggressive batching, heavy cache hit rate, and trimmed context lengths)

Notes / actions for MAP:
- We'll add three scenarios into the MAP workbook (conservative/typical/optimistic) and annotate which assumptions drive each (cache hit rate, batch latency target, tokenized prompt reduction).
- If HelixMed requires private deployment for PHI, add a separate pricing row: private infra premium (example +25–40% on per-token equivalent) due to reserved capacity and higher operational SLAs.
- Jordan will call out the SLA/loss-of-availability fallback in the MAP so procurement understands risk-adjusted unit economics.

I've attached the quick workbook (unit-econ-scan.xlsx) with the scenario tables. If you can confirm typical concurrency and an example traffic spike, we will populate the MAP sensitivity table and re-issue the MAP-draft by Thursday EOD.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Field Economics | Redwood Inference
[attachment: unit-econ-scan.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Sam Park <sam.park@helixmed.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: unit cost assumptions — can you confirm?

Thanks, Ben/Tessa — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick confirmations: 

- Traffic profile: typical triage window ~120 r/s, expected peak bursts up to ~320 r/s for <5 minutes during high volume events.
- For the eval/demo we will plan with the "typical" tokens/request (150k tokens/$) but procurement wants conservative and optimistic rows shown.
- HelixMed will require VPC/private deployment for the production pilot (PHI). Please add the private deployment premium row and an estimated delta to the MAP on Thursday.

Let's take the Friday 09:30 PT slot you suggested — Tessa, please send calendar invite. If procurement needs earlier escalation we'll route to legal but this looks on-track for our close timeline.

Sam
